$comment: Why this case is in the corpus: it is the only stored report containing a `**Row**:` line with no
`**Location**:` line above it, so it is the only case that pins the `location = null` reset
findingsFromReport performs after it pairs one. Delete that reset and every other case still
reproduces, while this one flips from unmeasurable to a scored result whose tenth finding sits at a
location it inherited from the ninth. Inventing a finding at a line the reviewer never cited is the
rubric's own fabricated-location penalty, arriving through the scorer instead of through the report.
It closes the same gap partially-attributed does as well, since nine attributed against ten declared is
also strictly between zero and the declared count. The two are kept apart because they store different
shapes: one is a violation summarized in prose, the other is a malformed finding block.
The report is CONSTRUCTED, from full-recall's report with a tenth block added. The shape is real:
test/fixtures/test-review-cli/reports/finding-without-location.md exists because a finding with a row
and no location is something reports actually contain.
derivation: The verdict declares 4 Critical, 4 High, 1 Medium and 1 Low, which sums to 10.
The report carries ten finding blocks. Nine pair a Location line with a Row line: C1, C3, C4, C5, H1,
H3, H4, H10 and L1, all at the lines their rules fire on. The tenth cites Row M3 and gives no location.
findingsFromReport walks the report line by line. It holds a location when it sees one and pushes a
finding when a Row line arrives while a location is held, then clears the location. By the time the M3
Row line arrives the location from L1 has already been cleared, so nothing is pushed. Nine findings are
9 is fewer than 10, so findingsFromReport returns null and scoreVerdict returns null with it.
Without the clear, the M3 Row would inherit L1's location and push a tenth finding at
seeded/checkout.spec.ts:19. Ten attributed against ten declared passes the guard, so the case would
score: hits 9, reported 10, unattributed 1, all of it resting on a line the report never associated
The two parsers disagree about this report by exactly one finding and that is correct. The CLI's
extractFindings reads block structure, so it counts the M3 block and puts a tenth entry in the verdict
with a null file and a null line. findingsFromReport reads adjacency, so it counts nine. Recall needs a
line to compare against and a finding with no location cannot supply one, which is why the stricter
count is the one that decides whether the run is scoreable.
The verdict's own numbers come from cli/lib/parse-report.js reading this report:
100 - 4x10 - 4x5 - 1x2 - 1x1 = 37, and any Critical at all forces Block.
